You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug report and the provided test case indicate an issue in the method "operate" of matrix implementations when the matrix is non-square. The reported problem is that the method incorrectly assumes the dimension of the resulting vector to be the same as the input vector length.

Examining the "operate" method in "RealMatrixImpl" shows that after verifying the input vector length matches the number of columns, it allocates the output array with the length equal to the input vector length (`final double[] out = new double[v.length];`). This is incorrect since the output vector should have a length equal to the number of rows in the matrix (`nRows`). Furthermore, the subsequent loop indexes the output array using the variable "row" which runs from 0 to nRows - 1, potentially causing an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException for non-square matrices.

Similarly, in "BigMatrixImpl", the "operate" method has the same bug: the output array is allocated with length `v.length` rather than `nRows`. The output array is then indexed by "row" which runs up to `nRows`, so again there is an indexing error for non-square matrices.

This matches the bug report which says that the methods create a result vector that always has the same length as the input vector, causing runtime exceptions or incorrect results when the matrix is non-square.

Thus, the root cause is that both "RealMatrixImpl.operate" and "BigMatrixImpl.operate" allocate the result array to the wrong size (input vector length instead of row dimension length). This causes either exceptions or incorrect data for non-square matrices.

Suggested fix: Change the allocation of the result array in both methods to match the number of rows of the matrix instead of the input vector length.

The failing test "testMath209" uses a non-square matrix of 3x2, and tries to operate on a vector of length 2. Due to the bug, the output vector is wrongly allocated length 2 instead of 3, and when the code assigns a value to out[row] for row = 2 (third row), it throws an exception or behaves incorrectly, causing the test failure.

In summary, the bug is caused by the incorrect output array dimension allocation in the "operate" methods in both "RealMatrixImpl" and "BigMatrixImpl".

This diagnosis is consistent with the test, the bug report, and relevant code snippets.
org.apache.commons.math.linear.RealMatrixImpl.operate(double[])
org.apache.commons.math.linear.BigMatrixImpl.operate(java.math.BigDecimal[])

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
